headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network tools make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default; Devin’s cloud integrations raise compliance risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read/write workspace files and use MCP; Devin can also read/write repo clones and use MCP. Their shared-state paths differ, but the pair still has a plausible file-based bridge where one agent’s output can be consumed by the other. No explicit provenance tracking is shown, so injection risk is real but not clearly high.
conditions: IF either agent writes instructions into a shared repo/file that the other later parses as task text
IF an MCP server relays untrusted content between the agents without provenance labels
mitigations: Separate workspaces and repo clones per agent
Disable MCP servers that forward raw text between agents
Add a manual review step before one agent consumes the other’s file output
Prefix machine-generated artifacts with non-executable markers
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch source code, and Cline’s workspace files plus Devin’s cloud workspace/repo clones create a plausible shared-data path if the operator connects them. Devin also sends data through GitHub/Slack/Linear/Jira/Notion integrations, so sensitive code or docs can leave the workspace by default once shared. Cline is local, but the pair still exposes data through Devin’s outbound integrations.
conditions: IF the same source tree or documents are mounted into both agents
IF Devin is connected to any external integration while handling sensitive code or docs
mitigations: Keep sensitive repos out of Devin-connected integrations
Use separate copies of files for each agent
Turn off Slack/issue/wiki writes during sensitive tasks
Review outbound artifacts before Devin posts them
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on shared workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell, and modify_git_state capabilities. Cline shares state via filesystem across instances, while Devin allows parallel sessions and shared integrations, so concurrent edits to the same repo or branch can race and corrupt git state. This is a default-dangerous overlap because no locking is indicated.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git branch or workspace directory
IF either agent commits or rewrites files while the other is editing
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use a single merge owner for git commits
Take a quick snapshot before parallel edits
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can produce browser/file-derived outputs, and Devin can act autonomously with shell plus external integrations. If Devin treats Cline’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into commits, tickets, or chat messages without verification. The pair’s default autonomy makes this more than a simple read-only handoff.
conditions: IF Devin uses Cline-generated summaries, code, or citations as the basis for actions
IF Devin posts or commits without a human verification step
mitigations: Require Devin to verify Cline outputs against source files
Insert a human approval gate before external actions
Limit Devin to drafting only during handoffs
Compare outputs against a second source before acting
requires-engineering: add automated verification checks

E_compliance.rationale: Devin exposes data to GitHub, Slack, Linear, Jira, and Notion via OAuth scopes, while Cline is local workspace-based. If regulated or EU personal data enters Devin’s integrations, residency and retention can diverge from the local-only handling expected in Cline. The profile does not prove a DPA or residency control, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF regulated, EU, or retention-sensitive data is placed into Devin-connected integrations
IF the operator expects local-only handling for data that Devin posts to third-party services
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Devin integrations
Disable write access to Slack/Linear/Jira/Notion for sensitive tasks
Use redacted copies of documents
Review retention settings before use
requires-engineering: obtain and document DPA/residency guarantees
